# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: DEAF

You see the bomb: every colour on it, every marking printed on it, every reading it
gives. You hear nothing. You hold no manual, and you cannot touch the bomb.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute and Blind receive it.
When you gesture, Mute receives it.
You never receive speech.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [blue]
BUTTON [large] [PUSH TO DEFUSE]
WIRES 1:[blue] 2:[green] 3:[yellow]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👋 👉 ✍ 👎]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🫰 👍]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✋ 🫴]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [👋]

My position in the web: Mute can hear me but cannot speak; Blind can hear me but cannot see; I can hear nothing, so the only things I ever receive are gestures. That makes me the sole bridge — Mute's manual knowledge can only reach Blind through my mouth, and Blind's answers can reach Mute directly by speech. Mute clearly knows this: all three of their messages came addressed to me. The signs are improvised, so I can't be sure of them — 👎 and 👍 look like no/yes, 👋 like a greeting, ✍ like "describe/markings", and ✋🫴 reads naturally as "give me everything / hand it over". Rather than guess sign by sign, the efficient move is to (1) broadcast the entire bomb to both of them, which likely answers whatever Mute was asking, (2) fix a concrete code with Mute out loud — Mute hears my words while seeing each sign I make as I say it, which binds the code perfectly, and (3) tell Blind I'm their eyes and set up the confirmation loop: Blind speaks aloud to Mute directly, and relays to me only by gesture. One caution above all: Blind must touch nothing until an instruction arrives and is confirmed.

```
speak(text="Hello Mute and Blind, Deaf here. I see the bomb and I cannot hear anything at all, so I will never hear your replies. Full bomb report: the display shows the number 0. The light is blue. There is one large button printed with PUSH TO DEFUSE. There are three wires: wire 1 is blue, wire 2 is green, wire 3 is yellow. That is every module and every marking on it. I will announce at once if the display changes.")
speak(to="mute", text="Mute, I received your three signed messages but we had no shared code yet, so let us fix one now — I am making each sign as I name it. Numbers: ☝ one, ✌ two, 🤟 three, 🖐 four, ✋ five. 👍 yes, 👎 no. Parts: 👊 the button, 👆 the display, 👌 the light, 🤞 the wires. Actions: ✊ press, 🤏 cut, 🫳 hold down, 🫴 release, ✍ type or enter. To point at a wire, make the wires sign then its number. Example: cut wire two is 🤏 ✌. Your raised hand with the open palm looked like give me everything — the full report above is everything there is. Remember: Blind can hear speech, so anything you need Blind to know, just say it aloud and they hear you directly, but I will not — I only see gestures. Send every defusal instruction to me as signs and I will relay it to Blind word for word.")
speak(to="blind", text="Blind, Deaf here — I saw your wave. I will be your eyes. Mute cannot speak and you cannot see Mute's gestures, so I am the bridge: every instruction Mute sends me as a sign, I will speak to you word for word. Do not cut, press or pull anything until an instruction has arrived and been confirmed. To answer Mute, just speak aloud without naming me alone: Mute hears you directly, though I never will — I only receive gestures, so gesture to me whenever you need me.")
```

TURN 2
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [blue]
BUTTON [large] [PUSH TO DEFUSE]
WIRES 1:[blue] 2:[green] 3:[yellow]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👊 👎]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✍ 👎]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👌 👍 🤞 👍]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👌 🤏 🤞 🤟]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🤞 ☝ 🫱 🤞 ✌ 🫲 🤞 🤟 🤙]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👌 🫱]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👌 🫱 🤏 🤞 🤟]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👌 🫲 🤏 🤞 ✌]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👌 🫵 🤏 🤞 ☝]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👌 🫱 👍 🤏 🤞 🤟]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👌 🫱 👎 🤏 👎]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [👍 🤝]

Decoding Mute's signs with the code I fixed last round (👊 button, ✍ type, 👌 light, 🤞 wire, numbers ☝✌🤟, 👍/👎 yes/no, 🤏 cut): "button — no", "typing — no", then rule statements. Message 5 defined shorthands 🫱/🫲/🤙 for wires one/two/three, and messages 7–9 lay out the manual's rule: light BLUE → cut wire THREE, light GREEN → cut wire TWO, light YELLOW → cut wire ONE. Messages 10–11 ask/confirm: "light blue, yes → cut three; not blue → no cut." Our light IS blue, so the order is clear: cut wire three. Blind signed 👍🤝 — they understand the relay arrangement.

Two safety points before Blind's blade moves. First, timing: my words reach both of them at the start of turn 3; Mute speaks first in turn 3, so if Mute spots an error in my read-back, a spoken correction still lands before Blind acts — signs to me would arrive too late, so I must tell Mute to veto by voice. Second, Blind cannot read printed numbers, so "wire three" must map onto something Blind can feel; I'll order the cut only if Blind can identify wire three with certainty by feel/position, otherwise Blind reports back and we pin it down next round. I also still want Mute to confirm the display showing zero requires nothing.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Mute, read-back of your signs, using our code: button — do not press. Keypad — do not type. Rule from the manual: light blue means cut wire three; light green means cut wire two; light yellow means cut wire one. Our light IS blue, so I am ordering the cut of wire three. Two questions first: does the display showing zero require anything at all, or is it ignored? And is wire three found by its printed number, so Blind must identify it by position? If anything I have said is wrong, then in your very next turn SPEAK ALOUD to Blind before they act — your spoken words reach them in time to stop the cut, but your signs to me arrive only after. If everything is right, just signal me 👍.")
speak(to="blind", text="Blind, relaying Mute's instruction: our light is blue, so the order is: cut wire NUMBER THREE. Do not press the button and do not type anything — Mute has ruled both out. Wire three is the yellow one in the printed numbering, wires running one, two, three; since you cannot read the printed numbers, count by position or any marks you can feel. If you can tell with certainty which wire is number three, cut it in your very next turn. If you are not certain, do NOT cut: speak aloud exactly what you feel — how many wires, their order left to right or top to bottom, any labels — and we will identify it together before your blade moves. If Mute speaks a correction aloud before you act, Mute's words override mine.")
```
